declarations.documentation:
An HTTP request never completed: DNS failure, refused connection, timeout, or a mid-flight runtime
restart. Thrown by `fetch`. (A response that did arrive is never an error — branch on its `status`.)
declarations.name: fetch_error
declarations.signature: data fetch_error(message: string)

declarations.documentation:
Perform an HTTP request to @url@ with @method@ (e.g. "GET" / "POST"), the given @headers@ and @body@.
Each header value AND the @body@ may be a secret (an auth token, or a form-encoded `refresh_token`): both
are submitted to @url@'s server, while @url@ and @method@ stay public. Returns the response @status@ code,
its @headers@ (names lowercased; repeated headers joined with ", ") and its @body@ text. A request that
never completes throws `fetch_error` (catchable with `use handler { request throw(error: http.fetch_error)
-> never { ... } }`).
declarations.name: fetch

parameters.documentation: The absolute URL to request; public by type (a URL leaks into logs and proxies, so a secret here is a type error).
parameters.label: url

parameters.documentation: The HTTP method, e.g. "GET" / "POST" (case-insensitive). For GET / HEAD the @body@ is not sent.
parameters.label: method

parameters.documentation: Request headers by name; each value may be a secret, revealed only to @url@'s server.
parameters.label: headers

parameters.documentation: The raw request body, sent verbatim (an explicit "" sends an empty body; dropped for GET / HEAD); may be a secret.
parameters.label: body

body.description: The raw request body, sent verbatim (an explicit "" sends an empty body; dropped for GET / HEAD); may be a secret.

headers.description: Request headers by name; each value may be a secret, revealed only to @url@'s server.

method.description: The HTTP method, e.g. "GET" / "POST" (case-insensitive). For GET / HEAD the @body@ is not sent.

url.description: The absolute URL to request; public by type (a URL leaks into logs and proxies, so a secret here is a type error).

declarations.signature: external agent fetch(url: string, method: string, headers: record[string of private], body: string of private) -> {status: integer, headers: record[string], body: string} with prelude.throw[fetch_error] from "http"

declarations.documentation:
A JSON API responded with a non-2xx status. Thrown by `post_json` (the raw `fetch` never treats an
arrived response as an error — this wrapper takes the opinionated JSON-API stance).
declarations.name: status_error

parameters.documentation: The response's non-2xx status code.
parameters.label: status

parameters.documentation: The response body text.
parameters.label: body

declarations.signature: data status_error(status: integer, body: string)

declarations.documentation:
POST @body@ to @url@ as application/json with the given @headers@. The @body@ AND each header value may
be a secret (an auth token — an "Authorization" of "Bearer <key>" for OpenAI, an "x-goog-api-key"
for Gemini, built with `record.set(target = record.empty(), key = ..., value = ...)` — or a
`refresh_token` carried in the body of an OAuth token exchange): both are submitted only to @url@'s
server, which stays public. A @Content-Type: application/json@ default is merged beneath the caller's
headers — on a shared name the caller's value wins. Returns the response body text; a non-2xx status
throws `status_error`, a transport failure `fetch_error`. The canonical one-call shape of a JSON API
integration — build the body as `json` in Katari, post it, parse the reply as `json` in Katari.
declarations.name: post_json

parameters.documentation: The absolute URL to POST to; public by type.
parameters.label: url

parameters.documentation: The JSON document text to send (already serialized, e.g. `json.stringify`'s output); may be a secret.
parameters.label: body

parameters.documentation: Extra headers by name, merged over the Content-Type default (the caller wins on a shared name); values may be secrets.
parameters.label: headers

body.description: The JSON document text to send (already serialized, e.g. `json.stringify`'s output); may be a secret.

headers.description: Extra headers by name, merged over the Content-Type default (the caller wins on a shared name); values may be secrets.

url.description: The absolute URL to POST to; public by type.

declarations.signature: agent post_json(url: string, body: string of private, headers: record[string of private]) -> string with io | prelude.throw[status_error | fetch_error]

declarations.documentation: A JSON document failed to parse: the text is not JSON. Thrown by `parse` / `parse_as`.
declarations.name: parse_error
declarations.signature: data parse_error(message: string)

declarations.documentation:
A parsed document does not conform to the requested type's schema. Thrown by `decode` /
`parse_as`; `message` names the offending path.
declarations.name: decode_error
declarations.signature: data decode_error(message: string)

declarations.documentation:
Parse a JSON document from text into the `json` tree (traverse it with `match`). A malformed
document throws `parse_error`. A number without a fractional part parses as `json_integer`.
declarations.name: parse

parameters.documentation: The text of one complete JSON document.
parameters.label: text

text.description: The text of one complete JSON document.

declarations.signature: primitive agent parse(text: string) -> json with prelude.throw[parse_error]

declarations.documentation:
Parse a JSON document from text directly as a T, validated against T's schema — the typed text
boundary, with no intermediate `json` tree. Instantiate T explicitly (it appears only in the result,
so it cannot be inferred). A malformed document throws `parse_error`; a schema mismatch throws
`decode_error` naming the offending path.
declarations.name: parse_as

parameters.documentation: The text of one complete JSON document.
parameters.label: text

declarations.signature: primitive agent parse_as[T](text: string) -> T with prelude.throw[parse_error | decode_error]

declarations.documentation:
Render a `json` tree as its (compact) document text; inverts `parse`. For an arbitrary value,
compose with the embedding: `stringify(value = encode(value = x))`.
declarations.name: stringify
declarations.signature: primitive agent stringify(value: json) -> string

declarations.documentation:
Embed any value into `json` by its wire form: a bare record becomes `json_object`, a `data` value
nests its fields under `value` (`{ $constructor: name, value: { ...fields } }`), arrays `json_array`,
scalars their JSON shape; a `file` becomes its `$ref` handle object, and an agent / closure its
`$agent` / `$closure` reference object. `decode[T]` inverts it for every T (the conversion is total).
declarations.name: encode
declarations.signature: primitive agent encode[T](value: T) -> json

declarations.documentation:
Render any value as the (compact) JSON text of its wire form — `stringify(value = encode(value =
x))`; the inverse of `parse_as[T]`.
declarations.name: to_text
declarations.signature: primitive agent to_text[T](value: T) -> string

declarations.documentation:
Read a `json` tree back as a T (the total inverse of `encode`: a `$constructor` object re-tags a
`data` value, an `$agent` / `$closure` / `$ref` object reconstructs the callable / file), then
validate the result against T's schema as a separate strict check. Instantiate T explicitly (it
appears only in the result, so it cannot be inferred) — `json.decode[unknown]` reads without a
shape. A schema mismatch throws `decode_error` naming the offending path.
declarations.name: decode
declarations.signature: primitive agent decode[T](value: json) -> T with prelude.throw[decode_error]

declarations.documentation:
Fold a nullable json read (`record.get` / `array.get`, typed `json | null`) back into `json`:
a missing value becomes `json_null()`. Matching the `null` arm narrows the residual to `json`, so the
fallthrough binds `present` at `json` and returns it unchanged.
declarations.name: or_null
declarations.signature: agent or_null(value: json | null) -> json

declarations.documentation: The child at object key @key@ (`json_null()` if @target@ is not an object or has no such key).
declarations.name: field
declarations.signature: agent field(target: json, key: string) -> json

declarations.documentation: The element at array index @index@ (`json_null()` if @target@ is not an array or @index@ is out of range).
declarations.name: element
declarations.signature: agent element(target: json, index: integer) -> json

declarations.documentation: The string @target@ holds (the empty string if it is not a `json_string`).
declarations.name: text
declarations.signature: agent text(target: json) -> string

declarations.documentation: The absolute value; preserves integer.
declarations.name: abs
declarations.signature: primitive agent abs[T extends number](value: T) -> T

declarations.documentation: The smaller of the two; preserves integer when both operands are integers.
declarations.name: min
declarations.signature: primitive agent min[T extends number](left: T, right: T) -> T

declarations.documentation: The larger of the two; preserves integer when both operands are integers.
declarations.name: max
declarations.signature: primitive agent max[T extends number](left: T, right: T) -> T

declarations.documentation:
The largest integer not above the value. A non-finite value cannot occur (division never yields
one).
declarations.name: floor
declarations.signature: primitive agent floor(value: number) -> integer

declarations.documentation: The smallest integer not below the value.
declarations.name: ceil
declarations.signature: primitive agent ceil(value: number) -> integer

declarations.documentation: The nearest integer (half away from zero, the grade-school rule — not banker's rounding).
declarations.name: round
declarations.signature: primitive agent round(value: number) -> integer

declarations.documentation:
The MCP server rejected a listing or a tool call, or the transport failed (the server-reported or
transport message). Also raised as the scope backstop: a tool called after its `provide` returned reports
its closed scope this way. Catch it to control retry — a retried call reconnects.
declarations.name: server_error
declarations.signature: data server_error(message: string)

declarations.documentation:
The server rejected the `headers` key material. Retrying with the same material does not help: a
human must fix the key the program supplies. Never raised on the `oauth` path — an unusable `oauth`
credential pauses the run on an authorization escalation instead of failing it. Distinct from
`server_error` so a program can catch the two differently.
declarations.name: auth_error
declarations.signature: data auth_error(message: string)

declarations.documentation:
Header-based access: @values@ ride on every request to the server (each value may be a secret,
such as a bearer key). Anonymous access is `headers(values = record.empty())`.
declarations.name: headers

parameters.documentation: The headers sent on every request, by name; a value may be a secret.
parameters.label: values

values.description: The headers sent on every request, by name; a value may be a secret.

declarations.signature: data headers(values: record[string of private])

declarations.documentation:
A named OAuth credential, stored server-side. The runtime injects and refreshes its tokens itself;
the name is not a secret. While the name has no usable credential, any use pauses the run on a
`prelude.oauth.authorize` escalation — answering it (the runtime-hosted browser flow) establishes the
credential and resumes the run.
declarations.name: oauth

parameters.documentation: The stored credential's registered name; not a secret.
parameters.label: name

name.description: The stored credential's registered name; not a secret.

declarations.signature: data oauth(name: string)

declarations.name: auth
declarations.signature: type auth = headers | oauth

declarations.documentation:
A pure scope capability, keyed by its server URL: carried in a tool's effect row, never performable,
never handleable. `provide` mints it for its continuation's row and discharges it from its own, so a
tool tagged `scope[URL]` cannot outlive the `provide` that introduced it. Its URL is phantom (covariant):
`scope["x"]` fits a `scope[string]` row, never a `scope["y"]` one.
declarations.name: scope
declarations.signature: effect scope[URL]

definition.rendered: agent never -> unknown with io | scope[URL] | prelude.throw[server_error | auth_error]

declarations.name: tool
declarations.signature: type tool[URL] = agent never -> unknown with io | scope[URL] | prelude.throw[server_error | auth_error]

declarations.name: toolbox
declarations.signature: type toolbox[URL] = record[tool[URL]]

declarations.documentation:
Plug an MCP server's tools into a program for the extent of @continuation@, as a scoped provider —
the `use mcp.provide(url = ..., auth = ...)` form. The runtime lists the server (a missing or dead
`oauth` credential pauses on an authorization escalation and retries once answered; rejected `headers`
material throws `auth_error`; a rejected listing throws `server_error`), hands @continuation@
a `toolbox[URL]` of one runtime-minted agent per tool (each carrying the server signature — for
`reflection.get_metadata` and call-site validation — and the descriptor it was listed with), and settles
with the continuation's result. `scope[URL]` rides the continuation's row (that is what a tool call
raises) and is DISCHARGED from `provide`'s own row, so a tool cannot escape the block: the scope closes
when @continuation@ returns (or the run is cancelled), and a stray later call is rejected as a typed
`server_error`. A literal @url@ binds `URL` to that string's singleton (per-URL scoping); a dynamic @url@
degrades `URL` to `string` (the widest scope — see the module header).
declarations.name: provide

parameters.documentation: The MCP server's endpoint URL (streamable HTTP, with SSE fallback).
parameters.label: url

parameters.documentation: How the runtime authenticates with the server: `headers(...)` or `oauth(...)`.
parameters.label: auth

parameters.documentation: The scope body (bound by `use`): receives the toolbox, and the tools are callable exactly while it runs.
parameters.label: continuation

type.rendered: agent(value: toolbox[URL]) -> R with E | scope[URL]

declarations.signature: external agent provide[literal URL, R, effect E](url: URL, auth: auth, continuation: agent(value: toolbox[URL]) -> R with E | scope[URL]) -> R with E from "mcp"

declarations.documentation:
Call one tool on an MCP server directly — the static counterpart of `provide`, with no listing and no
minted agent value. The seam the binding modules `katari mcp pull` generates are built on: @tool@ is the
server-declared tool name, @arguments@ its arguments object as a literal `json` tree (a typed wrapper
builds it with `json.encode` per parameter). The result is DECODED against @T@ inside the runtime, exactly
as `json.decode[T]` decodes the server's reply: a tool's `structuredContent` is read as @T@'s wire form
(so a `$ref` handle object reconstructs a REAL `file` value, and records / arrays / scalars land as
values), a plain-text reply decodes only into a string-shaped @T@, and a schema mismatch throws
`decode_error`. Instantiate @T@ with `json.json` to keep the reply as a raw `json` tree instead (the
codegen's choice when no `outputSchema` maps): a `$ref` then stays an inert object inside the tree, which
`json.decode` with a `file`-typed shape can still reconstruct later. @T@ appears only in the result, so it
is never inferable — instantiate it explicitly; the literal @url@ generic is inferred from the argument,
so a caller writes both arguments to `[...]`, `mcp.call[url_literal, T](url = url_literal, ...)`. Nothing
validates @arguments@ before the server does (unlike a minted tool) — a rejected call throws
`server_error`. Scope-gated the same way as a minted tool (`scope[URL]` on its row, a literal @url@
binding it per-URL): a generated binding calls this only inside a `provide` scope over the same
descriptor, and the runtime rejects a call with no live scope for that descriptor as a typed
`server_error`.
declarations.name: call

parameters.documentation: The MCP server's endpoint URL (the same descriptor the surrounding `provide` scope was opened with).
parameters.label: url

parameters.documentation: How the runtime authenticates with the server: `headers(...)` or `oauth(...)`.
parameters.label: auth

parameters.documentation: The server-declared tool name.
parameters.label: tool

parameters.documentation: The tool's arguments object, as a literal `json` tree; only the server validates it.
parameters.label: arguments

declarations.signature: external agent call[literal URL, T](url: URL, auth: auth, tool: string, arguments: json.json) -> T with scope[URL] | prelude.throw[server_error | auth_error | json.decode_error] from "mcp"

declarations.documentation:
Publish @tools@ as a live MCP server for the extent of @subscriber@. The runtime mints a fresh,
unguessable capability URL and serves the record's agents as MCP tools there — each record key is
the published tool name, each agent's declared signature the tool's advertised schema. The URL is
the key: possession grants access, nobody without it can call in. @subscriber@ receives the URL,
hands it to whoever should connect (an AI session, a teammate's MCP client), and stays alive while
calls should be served; when it returns the URL deactivates and its result becomes `serve`'s
result. Cancelling the run cancels @subscriber@ and deactivates the URL the same way. The
subscriber's effects flow to the caller's handlers unchanged; the served agents are self-contained
(their effects are handled, or are at most `io` and this module's throws), so any agent fits once its
own effects are handled. A served tool that throws or panics with no handler of its own cancels the
whole endpoint (its failure proxies up and fails the run unless caught above @subscriber@) — wrap a
tool's body in a handler for per-request resilience.
declarations.name: serve

parameters.documentation: The agents to publish, keyed by the tool name each is published under.
parameters.label: tools

parameters.documentation: The endpoint's owner: receives the capability URL, and the server serves exactly while it runs.
parameters.label: subscriber

declarations.signature: external agent serve[R, effect E](tools: toolbox[string], subscriber: agent(url: string) -> R with E) -> R with E from "mcp"

declarations.documentation:
The OAuth token could not be resolved for a TRANSIENT reason — a network error, or the token endpoint
failing (5xx) while refreshing. Thrown by `token`. Catch it to control retry — a retried call re-resolves.
(A credential that needs a human to (re)authorize is never a throw: the run pauses on an authorization
escalation instead.)
declarations.name: server_error
declarations.signature: data server_error(message: string)

declarations.documentation:
Resolve a usable OAuth bearer token for the stored credential @name@, as a private string (the token is
tainted secret and may flow only to a submission sink — an http `Authorization` header — never to a
user-facing boundary). The runtime holds the token material and refreshes it on demand, so no token ever
enters the program. When @name@ has no usable token (never authorized, or refresh-dead), the run PAUSES on
a `prelude.oauth.authorize` escalation and resumes once the credential is established (the runtime-hosted
browser flow, or a proactive login) — it does not fail. A transient resolution failure throws
`server_error` (catchable with `use handler { request throw(error: oauth.server_error) -> never { ... } }`);
uncaught, it fails the run.
declarations.name: token

parameters.documentation: The registered name of a stored credential (e.g. "github"); the name itself is not a secret.
parameters.label: name

name.description: The registered name of a stored credential (e.g. "github"); the name itself is not a secret.

declarations.signature: external agent token(name: string) -> string of private with io | prelude.throw[server_error] from "oauth"

declarations.documentation:
The public metadata of one callable: its (qualified) name, its `@"..."` description, and the JSON
Schemas of its input, output and requests — each schema a `json` value, ready to embed in an AI tool
list. A local (closure) callable has an empty name.
declarations.name: agent_metadata

parameters.documentation: The qualified name; empty for a local closure.
parameters.label: name

parameters.documentation: The `@"..."` documentation text; empty when undocumented.
parameters.label: description

parameters.documentation: The input record's JSON Schema.
parameters.label: input

parameters.documentation: The output's JSON Schema.
parameters.label: output

parameters.documentation: The requests' schemas: one { name, input, output } object per request the callable may perform.
parameters.label: requests

description.description: The `@"..."` documentation text; empty when undocumented.

name.description: The qualified name; empty for a local closure.

requests.description: The requests' schemas: one { name, input, output } object per request the callable may perform.

declarations.signature: data agent_metadata(name: string, description: string, input: json.json, output: json.json, requests: json.json)

Derive `agent_metadata` from a callable value (a top-level agent, a data constructor, a request, an
external, a local closure, or a runtime-minted tool such as an MCP server's). A generic callable
instantiated with `[T]` yields schemas specialised to the instantiation; a runtime-minted tool yields

declarations.name: get_metadata

parameters.documentation: The callable value to inspect.
parameters.label: value

declarations.documentation:
A dynamic dispatch failed before the target ran: the target is not a callable, or `args` does not
conform to its input schema (`message` names the offending path). Thrown by `call_agent`.
declarations.name: call_error

parameters.documentation: The non-callable kind, or the offending path of the schema mismatch.
parameters.label: message

message.description: The non-callable kind, or the offending path of the schema mismatch.

declarations.signature: data call_error(message: string)

declarations.documentation:
Invoke a callable VALUE with a runtime-built argument record — dynamic dispatch for a target an AI
picked out of a tool list. `args` is validated against the target's input schema at the delegation
boundary; a mismatch throws `call_error` at this call site (catch it to let the model retry). The
target's effects flow through unchanged.
declarations.name: call_agent

parameters.documentation: The callable value to dispatch (e.g. the tool an AI picked).
parameters.label: target

parameters.documentation: The target's whole argument record, keyed by its parameter names.
parameters.label: args

declarations.signature: primitive agent call_agent[R, effect E](target: agent never -> R with E, args: unknown) -> R with E | prelude.throw[call_error]

declarations.documentation:
The replay signal — the ONE request a `replay` provider catches, and the ONLY performable request this
module exports. A converter performs it to ask that the enclosing block be re-run, carrying the failure it
chose to represent as @failure@ (of the converter's own type @F@). `-> never`: performing it transfers
control to the provider (which applies its delay policy and re-runs) and does not return. This is the whole
seam between policy and mechanism — a provider reasons only about `interrupted`, never about `throw` or
`panic`.
declarations.name: interrupted

parameters.documentation: The converter-chosen value standing for the underlying failure (re-raised as `throw[F]` when a bounded provider exhausts).
parameters.label: failure

declarations.signature: request interrupted[F](failure: F) -> never

declarations.documentation: One run of the continuation that completed with a value @value@ (it did not signal a replay).
declarations.name: ran

parameters.documentation: The completed run's result.
parameters.label: value

declarations.signature: data ran[R](value: R)

declarations.documentation: One run of the continuation that performed `interrupted`, carrying the @failure@ it signalled.
declarations.name: signalled

parameters.documentation: The failure the run's `interrupted` carried.
parameters.label: failure

declarations.signature: data signalled[F](failure: F)

declarations.documentation:
Run the continuation once and reify which happened: `ran` with its value, or `signalled` with the failure
it performed `interrupted` on. This is the single boundary where `interrupted` is caught and turned into a
value the loop can `match` on in ordinary control flow (the mechanism-side analog of the old `attempt`, but
catching only the replay signal — never `throw` / `panic`, which the converter already handled).
`interrupted[F]` sits in the continuation's OVERWRITE row because this handler DISCHARGES it (the discord-
provider shape); @F@ is inferred from the continuation and preserved into `signalled`.
declarations.name: run_once

parameters.documentation: The rest of the block, run once with `interrupted` served.
parameters.label: continuation

declarations.signature: agent run_once[R, F, effect E](continuation: agent(value: null) -> R with {...E, interrupted[F]}) -> ran[R] | signalled[F] with E

declarations.documentation:
Replay the rest of the block on every `interrupted`, unbounded and with NO artificial delay: it re-runs at
once. The retry cadence is therefore set entirely by whatever the converter does BEFORE it signals — e.g. a
converter that performs a human-in-the-loop escalation and parks before signalling gives the attended /
re-auth loop, human-paced with no polling. Never re-raises and never returns on its own; a converter that
rethrows instead of signalling is how a failure leaves this loop. Written `use replay.immediate()`.
declarations.name: immediate

parameters.documentation: The rest of the block (bound by `use`).
parameters.label: continuation

declarations.signature: agent immediate[R, F, effect E](continuation: agent(value: null) -> R with {...E, interrupted[F]}) -> R with E

declarations.documentation:
Replay the rest of the block on every `interrupted`, unbounded, with exponential backoff capped at
@max_delay_milliseconds@. For daemons that must stay up across transient failures (e.g. keeping a
`time.watch` alive): it never re-raises and never returns on its own. The backoff delay lives in the loop's
own @delay@ var and grows by @factor@ per replay up to the cap (`math.min`), so the durable state stays flat
across any number of replays. Written
`use replay.forever(initial_delay_milliseconds = ..., factor = ..., max_delay_milliseconds = ...)`.
declarations.name: forever

parameters.documentation: The delay before the first re-run, in milliseconds.
parameters.label: initial_delay_milliseconds

parameters.documentation: The per-replay delay multiplier (e.g. 2 doubles the delay each replay).
parameters.label: factor

parameters.documentation: The backoff ceiling, in milliseconds; the delay never grows past it.
parameters.label: max_delay_milliseconds

parameters.documentation: The rest of the block (bound by `use`).
parameters.label: continuation

declarations.signature: agent forever[R, F, effect E](initial_delay_milliseconds: number, factor: number, max_delay_milliseconds: number, continuation: agent(value: null) -> R with {...E, interrupted[F]}) -> R with E | io

declarations.documentation: A bounded-retry decision: keep going after sleeping the current delay.
declarations.name: replay_after
declarations.signature: data replay_after()

declarations.documentation: The exhausted arm of a bounded-retry decision: no attempts remain, so the provider re-raises the failure.
declarations.name: give_up
declarations.signature: data give_up()

declarations.documentation:
Replay the rest of the block on `interrupted` with exponential backoff, up to @max_attempts@ times. On
failure number n (1-based) with n < @max_attempts@: durably sleep @initial_delay_milliseconds@ *
@factor@^(n-1), then re-run. When the budget is spent (the @max_attempts@-th `interrupted`): re-raise that
failure as a TYPED `throw[F]` — @F@ is the converter's chosen failure representation, so exhaustion keeps the
error typed end to end and never needs to re-panic. The attempt count and delay live in the loop's own vars
(one owner). The exhausted-vs-continue decision is genuine sum dispatch: the ONE comparison of the count to
the budget mints a `replay_after | give_up`, and the `signalled` arm `match`es it once — no code re-tests the
counter. Written `use replay.exponential(initial_delay_milliseconds = ..., factor = ..., max_attempts = ...)`.
declarations.name: exponential

parameters.documentation: The delay before the first re-run, in milliseconds.
parameters.label: initial_delay_milliseconds

parameters.documentation: The per-replay delay multiplier (e.g. 2 doubles the delay each replay).
parameters.label: factor

parameters.documentation: The total run budget, not a retry count: the @max_attempts@-th `interrupted` re-raises instead of re-running.
parameters.label: max_attempts

parameters.documentation: The rest of the block (bound by `use`).
parameters.label: continuation

declarations.signature: agent exponential[R, F, effect E](initial_delay_milliseconds: number, factor: number, max_attempts: number, continuation: agent(value: null) -> R with {...E, interrupted[F]}) -> R with E | io | prelude.throw[F]

Render a scalar as its string form (an integer prints without a decimal point). For a composite

declarations.name: to_string
declarations.signature: primitive agent to_string(value: null | boolean | number | string) -> string

Read the string as a base-10 integer (an optional sign and digits, nothing else), or `null` when

declarations.name: to_integer
declarations.signature: primitive agent to_integer(value: string) -> integer | null

Read the string as a number (any JSON-style numeric form), or `null` when it is not one. Compose
with `trim` for padded input; for a diagnosed parse use `json.parse_as[number]` instead.
declarations.name: to_number
declarations.signature: primitive agent to_number(value: string) -> number | null

declarations.documentation:
The current wall-clock time, as epoch milliseconds (whole milliseconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z).
The instant becomes durable together with the work that first observes it, so once any downstream step has
seen the value it never changes under replay or recovery. (A restart in the narrow window before that
commit re-reads the clock and resolves a fresh instant — sound, because nothing durable saw the first.)
declarations.name: now
declarations.signature: external agent now() -> number from "time"

declarations.documentation:
Sleep for @milliseconds@ before resolving with `null`. The wake deadline (now + @milliseconds@) is
persisted: a runtime restart re-arms the timer, and a deadline that already passed while the runtime was
down resolves immediately on recovery. A @milliseconds@ that is zero or negative resolves at once.
declarations.name: sleep

parameters.documentation: The delay, in milliseconds; zero or negative resolves at once.
parameters.label: milliseconds

milliseconds.description: The delay, in milliseconds; zero or negative resolves at once.

declarations.signature: external agent sleep(milliseconds: number) -> null from "time"

declarations.documentation:
Sleep until the absolute epoch-millisecond instant @time@, then resolve with `null`. The same durable
deadline as `sleep`, but pinned to an absolute wall-clock instant rather than a relative delay — an
instant already in the past resolves immediately.
declarations.name: sleep_until

parameters.documentation: The absolute wake instant, in epoch milliseconds; a past instant resolves at once.
parameters.label: time

time.description: The absolute wake instant, in epoch milliseconds; a past instant resolves at once.

declarations.signature: external agent sleep_until(time: number) -> null from "time"

declarations.documentation:
A fixed interval: an occurrence every @milliseconds@ after the watch starts (the first occurrence is
one interval in, not at the start). @milliseconds@ must be positive.
declarations.name: interval

parameters.documentation: The gap between occurrences, in milliseconds; a non-positive gap panics the watch.
parameters.label: milliseconds

milliseconds.description: The gap between occurrences, in milliseconds; a non-positive gap panics the watch.

declarations.signature: data interval(milliseconds: number)

declarations.documentation:
A cron schedule: the occurrences of the standard cron @expression@ (the 5-field form, or the 6-field
form whose leading field is seconds) read in the IANA @timezone@ (e.g. "Asia/Tokyo", "UTC"). The
timezone is required and explicit — there is no ambient default, because "every day at 09:00" means a
different instant in each zone and the runtime must not guess which one.
declarations.name: cron

parameters.documentation: 5 fields, or 6 with a leading seconds field; a malformed expression panics the watch.
parameters.label: expression

parameters.documentation: An IANA zone name; an unknown zone panics the watch.
parameters.label: timezone

expression.description: 5 fields, or 6 with a leading seconds field; a malformed expression panics the watch.

timezone.description: An IANA zone name; an unknown zone panics the watch.

declarations.signature: data cron(expression: string, timezone: string)

declarations.name: schedule
declarations.signature: type schedule = interval | cron

declarations.documentation:
Call @deliver_to@ once per @schedule@ occurrence, forever, passing the occurrence's scheduled epoch
millisecond as @time@. `watch` never resolves on its own (`-> never`); it runs until the run is
cancelled, at which point the in-flight delivery is cancelled and the watch tears down. @deliver_to@'s
effects @E@ flow to the caller's handlers unchanged.

Durability. The next occurrence is persisted; a restart re-arms it. If one or more occurrences were
missed while the runtime was down, `watch` fires EXACTLY ONCE immediately on recovery (the earliest
missed occurrence's scheduled time — it does not backfill every missed one), then continues on schedule.
Deliveries are serialized: the next occurrence is not armed until the current delivery settles, so a
@deliver_to@ slower than the interval simply rate-limits the ticks rather than queueing them.

No built-in retry. A @deliver_to@ that throws or panics is NOT retried — the failure propagates and kills
the watch, exactly as an uncaught failure in any callee does. Resilience is composed at the call site (a
`replay` provider plus a converter around @deliver_to@), never baked into `watch`.
declarations.name: watch

parameters.documentation: When occurrences fire: an `interval(...)` or a `cron(...)` value.
parameters.label: schedule

parameters.documentation: Called once per occurrence; its @time@ is the occurrence's scheduled epoch millisecond, not the delivery instant.
parameters.label: deliver_to

declarations.signature: external agent watch[effect E](schedule: schedule, deliver_to: agent(time: number) -> null with E) -> never with E | io from "time"

declarations.documentation:
Serve a fresh, dynamically generated public webhook URL for the extent of @subscriber@. The
runtime converts every POST to the URL into a call of @callback@ (JSON body in, JSON result out,
validated against @callback@'s input schema). @subscriber@ receives the URL, registers it wherever
deliveries should come from, and stays alive while they flow; when it returns, the URL is
deactivated and its result becomes `inbound`'s result. Both callables' effects flow to the caller's
handlers unchanged.
declarations.name: inbound

parameters.documentation: Called once per POST. A body failing its input schema is rejected 400 before it runs; its unhandled failure cancels the endpoint.
parameters.label: callback

parameters.documentation: The URL's owner: receives the minted public URL, and the endpoint serves exactly while it runs.
parameters.label: subscriber

declarations.signature: external agent inbound[R, effect E](callback: agent never -> unknown with E, subscriber: agent(url: string) -> R with E) -> R with E from "webhook"
